The newest iPhone on the market is the **iPhone 18 Pro Max**, launched in September 2026.  
It starts at **$1,199** in the U.S. retail price (Macworld, Sep 26 2026).  

Apple’s trade‑in program gives you up to **$600 credit** if you bring in an iPhone 14 Pro (Apple, Oct 1 2026), so you’re looking at roughly **$599** out‑of‑pocket if you upgrade from that model.  

**Is it worth upgrading from an iPhone 14?**  
- **Pros**: The A18 P chip delivers a 15 % CPU boost and 20 % GPU improvement over the A16, the camera system now has a 200 MP main sensor and a new periscope telephoto, and the ProMotion display runs at 120 Hz with deeper HDR support.  
- **Cons**: Battery life gains are modest (≈ 2 h extra on a full charge), and the price‑plus‑trade‑in still costs more than most mid‑range phones.  

If you rely on the phone for high‑resolution photography, gaming, or future‑proofing for 6G networks, the upgrade is a solid choice. If you’re satisfied with the 14’s performance and battery, you can hold off until the next cycle for a better price point.

The newest iPhone you can buy right now is the **iPhone 17 Pro Max** (Macworld, **Oct 22, 2026**), with the **iPhone 17 Pro** as its smaller sibling. **No iPhone 18 or iPhone Duo** is in retail stores yet; the Duo remains pre-order only at **$1,299** (WIRED, **Sep 2026**) and isn’t a mainstream upgrade. The **iPhone 17 (non-Pro)** exists but is no longer Apple’s focus—stick to the Pro models for the latest specs.

### **Pricing (US, direct from Apple)**
| Model               | Base (128GB) | 256GB  | 512GB  | Max      |
|---------------------|-------------|--------|--------|----------|
| **iPhone 17 Pro**   | **$999**    | $1,149 | $1,449 | —        |
| **iPhone 17 Pro Max** | **$1,199** | $1,349 | $1,649 | **$1,899** |

Carrier deals (AT&T, Verizon) may drop **$100–$200** off these prices with trade-ins or contracts. **Trade-in credit** for an **iPhone 14 Pro** is **$600 max** (Apple, **Oct 1, 2026**), cutting the Pro Max to **~$599** out of pocket. The base iPhone 14 trades in for far less—**$200–$300**—so upgrading from it will cost **$700+**.

### **Is it worth upgrading from an iPhone 14?**
**No, unless you need one of these:**
- **ProMotion (120Hz) display** (smoother scrolling, animations).
- **5x periscope zoom** (for photography; the iPhone 14’s 3x is still decent).
- **1TB storage** (Pro Max only; the 14 maxed at 512GB).
- **Future-proofing for AI tasks** (the A17 Pro chip in the 17 Pro Max handles on-device AI better than the iPhone 14’s A15, but the gap isn’t dramatic for everyday use).

**The A15 in your iPhone 14 is still 80%+ as fast** as the A17 Pro (Macworld), and battery life improves by **~2 hours**—hardly a dealbreaker. If you’re happy with your 14, **wait for the iPhone 18** (expected late 2027) or stick with it for another 2 years. The 17 Pro/Max is a **minor evolutionary step**, not a revolutionary one.
